newsitem.title: UK: Brent cash market steady to firmer ahead of expiry.
newsitem.headline: Brent cash market steady to firmer ahead of expiry.

text.p: The North Sea Brent paper market was talked steady to a shade firmer on Friday morning ahead of the expiry of the July IPE contract at the close of trade.
Intermonth spreads were actively traded early on, with July/August changing hands at -32 cents, -28 cents and -26 cents, having traded at -30 cents on Thursday.
The spread fetched -29 cents and -27 cents in the U.S. aftermarket.
CFDs for next week (June 16-20) were bid at August Brent -65 cents, while the following week (June 23-27) was bid some five cents firmer at August -51 cents.
The July Brent loading programme scheduled the equivalent of 40.5 cargoes, compared to 38.4 cargoes in June.
The heavier programme was attributed to the longer month in July and a lighter maintenance schedule.
Some traders said that an even bigger jump in volumes was expected, and the paper market was stronger as a consequence.
July Brent was trading 28 cents higher at $17.72 on the IPE screen at 1005 GMT, as investment funds baled out of their long positions ahead of the expiry.
"The paper is firmer on the back of the expiry of July and there's less Brent than people expected," said one paper trader.
Other traders said the loading programme was broadly in line with expectations.
"The majority of traders thought it was bang-on," said one.
But a slide in Gullfaks loadings by three cargoes to 21 cargoes in July was not anticipated by traders.
They said they were unaware of any maintenance plans which might account for the shortfall, but said it could be linked to technical problems at the Vigdis field.
